redness.label: Redness
redness.description: Skin redness (also called erythema) happens when tiny blood vessels near the surface of your skin get wider, so more blood flows there and the skin looks pink or red. You might have this concern if your cheeks, nose, or chin often look flushed, blotchy, or red, especially after washing your face, being in the heat, or using a new product.
causes: Skin conditions: Rosacea, eczema, and psoriasis can leave red, itchy, or flaky patches
Product reactions: Your skin can react badly to soaps, fragrances, or harsh ingredients
Sun and weather: Sunburn, heat, wind, and big temperature changes
Rubbing or scrubbing: Scrubbing too hard or over-exfoliating irritates the skin

acne.label: Acne
acne.description: Acne is when pores get blocked and turn into pimples. That includes whiteheads, blackheads, red bumps, and sometimes painful lumps under the skin. You might have this concern if you regularly get breakouts on your face, chest, or back, and not just one pimple every now and then.
causes: Extra oil: Your skin makes too much oil, and it gets stuck in pores
Dead skin buildup: Dead skin cells don’t shed properly and plug the pores
Bacteria: Germs that normally live on skin grow inside blocked pores and cause swelling
Hormones: Changes during puberty, periods, pregnancy, or stress can trigger breakouts
Pore-clogging products: Heavy makeup, oils, or hair products can block pores

antiAging.label: Anti-aging
antiAging.description: Anti-aging isn’t a problem in itself. It means caring for the signs of skin getting older, like fine-lines, wrinkles, sagging, and loss of bounce. You might care about this if you notice lines around your eyes or mouth, or if your skin feels less firm than it used to.
causes: Natural aging: Your body makes less collagen, the protein that keeps skin firm and bouncy, as you get older
Sun exposure: UV rays from the sun are the biggest outside cause of early wrinkles
Smoking: It breaks down collagen and reduces blood flow to the skin
Repeated facial movements: Squinting, frowning, and smiling over the years form lines
Lack of moisture: Dry skin makes fine lines look more noticeable

dryness.label: Dryness
dryness.description: Dry skin means your skin doesn’t have enough moisture or oil to stay soft. You might have this concern if your skin often feels tight (especially after washing), looks flaky or rough, or feels itchy.
causes: Weather: Cold air, low humidity, and wind pull moisture from your skin
Hot showers: Hot water strips away your skin’s natural oils
Harsh cleansers: Strong soaps remove too much oil
Not enough moisturizer: Skin loses water without something to lock it in
Genetics or age: Some people naturally have drier skin, and skin gets drier with age

darkSpots.label: Dark spots
darkSpots.description: Dark spots (also called hyperpigmentation) are flat patches that are darker than the rest of your skin. They happen when your skin makes too much melanin, the natural pigment that gives skin its color. You might have this concern if you see brown, tan, or dark marks that stay around, such as spots left behind after a pimple heals.
causes: Sun damage: Years of sun exposure can create “sun spots” or “age spots”
Leftover acne marks: Pimples can leave dark marks after they heal
Hormones: Pregnancy or birth control can cause patches called melasma
Skin injuries: Cuts, burns, bug bites, or picking at skin can leave dark marks

cloggedPores.label: Clogged pores
cloggedPores.description: Clogged pores happen when oil and dead skin get stuck inside the tiny openings in your skin. You might have this concern if you see blackheads (small dark dots, often on the nose), whiteheads, or tiny bumps that make your skin feel bumpy. Clogged pores aren’t always full-on acne, but they can turn into it.
causes: Too much oil: Oily skin is more likely to get pores blocked
Dead skin buildup: Skin that isn’t exfoliated can trap gunk in pores
Heavy products: Thick creams, oils, or makeup can sit in pores
Not washing properly: Leftover makeup, sweat, or dirt at the end of the day

texture.label: Texture
texture.description: Skin texture is how your skin feels and looks up close. “Texture problems” means it isn’t smooth. You might have this concern if your skin feels rough, bumpy, or uneven when you run your fingers over it, or if you see small bumps, enlarged pores, or acne scars.
causes: Dead skin buildup: Old skin cells piling up make skin feel rough
Acne scars: Past breakouts can leave dips or raised spots
Clogged pores: Tiny blocked pores create little bumps
Dryness: Dry, flaky skin feels rough
Sun damage and aging: Over time, skin can become less smooth and even

sensitiveSkin.label: Sensitive skin
sensitiveSkin.description: Sensitive skin means your skin reacts easily to things that don’t bother most people. You might have this concern if your skin often stings, burns, itches, or turns red after using new products, or if lots of products “don’t agree” with you.
causes: Weak skin barrier: Your skin’s outer protective layer is damaged and lets irritants in more easily
Fragrance and harsh ingredients: Perfumes, alcohol, and strong acids are common triggers
Skin conditions: Eczema, rosacea, and allergies make skin more reactive
Overdoing it: Using too many products or exfoliating too often
Weather: Cold, wind, and heat can set off reactions

dullness.label: Dullness
dullness.description: Dull skin looks tired, flat, or gray instead of fresh and glowing. You might have this concern if your skin doesn’t seem to reflect light, looks uneven in color, or people often say you look tired even when you’re not.
causes: Dead skin buildup: A layer of old skin cells hides the fresher skin underneath
Dehydration: Skin without enough water looks less plump and bright
Lack of sleep: Poor sleep can make skin look pale and tired
Sun damage: Over time, it makes skin tone uneven
Smoking and stress: Both reduce blood flow and healthy color in the skin

oiliness.label: Oiliness
oiliness.description: Oily skin means your skin makes more oil (called sebum) than it needs. You might have this concern if your face looks shiny or greasy a few hours after washing, especially on your forehead, nose, and chin (the “T-zone”), or if makeup tends to slide off.
causes: Genetics: Some people are simply born with oilier skin
Hormones: Puberty, periods, and stress can increase oil
Hot, humid weather: Skin produces more oil in heat
Over-washing: Stripping your skin too much can make it produce more oil to make up for it
Heavy products: Thick or greasy products can add to the shine
